newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Inquiry hears media rules antiquated - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Inquiry hears media rules antiquated - Canberra.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Wednesday many submissions to the government's media inquiry supported its views that the current rules were antiquated.

"To date it (the inquiry), has received 37 submissions, many of which support the government's views that the rules are antiquated and impractical," Alston told a Screen Production Association conference in Melbourne.
The inquiry was supposed to produce a discussion paper within a month or two with any legislative changes to follow.
Current regulations restrict investments in one form of media, such as television, by players with an interest in another, say newspapers.
Alston said: "What you have to concentrate on is not just the number of players but the number of different voices that are able to be expressed."
"If you are getting a balance of views then that's more important than simply looking at the number of owners."
The inquiry was not set up to consider the other major element of media regulation -- the limits on foreign investment.
However, that issue was raised in submissions by most of the big industry players.
